test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future continuous tense form.

Shall I meet you soon?

options.text: Shall I have met you soon?
Shall I be meeting you soon?
Will I be meeting you soon?

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Shall I be meeting you soon?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is asking about meeting someone in the future, and it needs to be expressed in the **future continuous tense**.
 
• Future continuous tense describes actions that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.
 
• The structure of the future continuous tense is **will/shall + be + present participle (verb + -ing)**.
 
• Option 2, **"Shall I be meeting you soon?"**, correctly follows this structure and expresses the action in future continuous tense.

Correct sentence: *Shall I be meeting you soon?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** will/shall + be + present participle (verb + -ing).
 
• **Example:** I will be working on the project tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will be ongoing at a particular time in the future.
 
 
 
• **Future Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** will/shall + base verb.
 
• **Example:** I will meet you tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will happen in the future but are not continuous.
